tools.name: clear_table_filter

If a call returns table_missing, table_hidden, or table_read_only, follow recovery_guidance and the live available_tables snapshot rather than repeating discovery or the failed call. Never substitute another dataset without user confirmation. Rebuild a call at most once after the target becomes available; if it fails again, explain the blocker.

table_key.description: The tableKey of a currently visible table. Available table keys are included in the message context and from list_page_tables.

tools.name: clear_table_filters
tools.description: Remove all user-applied filters from a visible table (locked filters are preserved). Sort, grouping, and columns are unchanged. If a call returns table_missing, table_hidden, or table_read_only, follow recovery_guidance and the live available_tables snapshot rather than repeating discovery or the failed call. Never substitute another dataset without user confirmation. Rebuild a call at most once after the target becomes available; if it fails again, explain the blocker.

tools.name: edit_procurement_report
tools.description: Edit sections of the live procurement report draft WITHOUT saving. Requires execution_id and expected_editor_revision from get_procurement_report_editor. Apply at most 20 edits per call; read again before each additional batch. Update only the requested sections; omitted header/body fields and all other sections are preserved. Preserve source citations and links. Put section headings in header, not body_markdown. Insert after a stable ID, or at the start with after_stable_id=null. Remove deletes only that section. Edits apply atomically and fail if the user changed the draft since your read. Read again after a conflict. Never claim changes are saved; the user reviews the editor and clicks Save.

tools.name: get_current_page_context
tools.description: Read the page the user is currently viewing in Ramp: path, title, context_version, functional_client_tools, and any capabilities currently registered by that page. Use this again after navigation or after a table/form tool reports that its target is unavailable. Leave kinds and ids blank to get all registered page capabilities.

kinds.description: Only return page capabilities with one of these kinds. Leave blank to get all registered page capabilities.

ids.description: Only return page capabilities with one of these ids. Leave blank to get all registered page capabilities.

tools.name: get_form_schema
tools.description: Read the schema of a form open on the user's screen: fields with labels, kinds, current values, validation errors, and selectable options (option tokens). A form is open ONLY when it is listed as a `form` surface in the current page context (the page_capabilities hint sent with the message, or get_current_page_context). If no `form` surface is listed, no form is open — there is nothing to read, so do not call this. Call it before filling a listed form. Omit form_id only for initial discovery when exactly one form is open and no intended form_id is already known. Keep using the intended form_id after failures; never omit or replace it to recover from a closed-form error.

form_id.description: The open form to target, from get_current_page_context form capabilities. Optional only for initial discovery when exactly one form is open and no intended form_id is already known. Keep using the intended form_id once known; never omit or replace it to recover from a closed-form error.

tools.name: get_procurement_report_editor
tools.description: Read the procurement report open in the fullscreen editor, including unsaved changes, section stable IDs, and editor_revision. Read before editing. The execution_id comes from the procurement_agent_report_editor page capability. This is the report, not the agent instructions or request fields.

tools.name: get_skill_editor_state
tools.description: Read the live state of the skill editor open on the user's screen: editor kind, name, description, read-only reference material, and the full document as markdown, including unsaved edits. Call this before editing so you work with the user's current draft rather than the last saved version.

tools.name: get_spend_program_editor_state
tools.description: Read the live state of the spend program editor open on the user's screen: program shape, every settings section in the shape set_spend_program_settings accepts, the names and available choices behind referenced ids (policies, merchant categories, accounting coding), approval and change request workflow pointers, custom request form questions (intake) and change order form questions (change_request_intake, purchase order programs only) with their ids, and editor_revision. Includes unsaved edits. Call this before the first write and again after a revision conflict.

tools.name: prepare_spend_program_workflow_edit

Use form="request" for approval workflows and form="change_request" for dedicated change request workflows. Change request preparation saves the request form first. Await success, then pass the returned template_id and custom_form_collection_log_entry_uuid to GetBlankCanvasConditionFields and ApplyBlankCanvasWorkflowEdits. The template_id is resolved after preparation; use it instead of earlier editor or autosave pointers. Prepare again after question edits; discard cached condition fields when the returned revision changes. On failure, reread the editor and prepare again rather than falling back to published questions. Does not save or publish the program or edit the workflow.

tools.name: set_spend_program_intake_questions
tools.description: Create, name, rename, or remove request form sections and add, update, or remove custom questions in the spend program editor open on the user's screen WITHOUT saving. Requesting programs only. form selects the target: request (default) edits the request form and takes ids from intake.sections; change_request edits the change order form requesters fill in when changing an approved request and takes ids from change_request_intake.sections, which only purchase order programs have. Read the target form from get_spend_program_editor_state first: it lists every question with its id, and built-in fields you must not duplicate. Section operations are only supported for form=request. add_section names the sole untitled section if present, preserving its questions, or appends a new section. update_section names or renames an existing section by section_id while preserving its id, questions, and conditions. remove_section deletes the section and all its questions and clears dependent visibility or required-when rules, including change order rules. A section containing a protected question cannot be removed. Removing the last section leaves a fresh empty untitled section. Create sections first, then use created_section_ids from the result as section_id when adding questions. If the request form uses sections, every section must have a meaningful, nonblank title and at least one question before saving or publishing. When organizing a form into sections, use update_section to name any existing unnamed sections. A sole section with title=null is the default unsectioned form and may remain unnamed and empty, including after removing the last section. Leave new question descriptions blank unless the user explicitly requests them; do not repeat the question title. Only add question types listed in that form's available_question_types; other types are rejected for this program. Select choices carry ids: when replacing a question's choices, pass { id, label } for every choice you keep or rename so visibility rules that depend on it keep working, and a bare string only for new choices. Operations apply in order; a visibility rule may only reference an earlier BOOLEAN or select question by id, so add controlling questions first and use the ids this tool returns. Requires the editor_revision from a fresh read. Returns the merged questions with ids and the form's validation errors. Never claim to have saved.

form.description: Which form to edit. request: the request form (ids from intake.sections). change_request: the change order form requesters fill in when changing an approved request (ids from change_request_intake.sections); only purchase order programs have one.

operations.description: Applied in order. Create sections first, then use their returned ids to add questions. Add a controlling question in one call and reference its returned id before adding dependent questions.

title.description: Section heading for the request form only. Names the sole untitled section if one exists, preserving its questions; otherwise appends a new section. Use the returned created_section_ids to add questions in a subsequent call. Every section needs at least one question before saving or publishing.

section_id.description: Section id from intake.sections in get_spend_program_editor_state.

title.description: Name or rename a request form section, preserving its id, questions, and conditions.

section_id.description: Section id from intake.sections. Removes the request form section and all its questions. Rejected if any contained question cannot be deleted. Rules depending on deleted questions are cleared, including change order rules. Removing the last section leaves a fresh empty untitled section.

title.description: Question shown to requesters. Unique per type within a section.

description.description: Helper text under the question. Leave blank unless the user explicitly requests it; do not repeat the title.

choices.description: Choice labels, in order. Only for TEXT_SINGLE_SELECT and TEXT_MULTI_SELECT.

visible_when.description: Show this question only when an earlier answer matches.

question_id.description: id of an EARLIER question of type BOOLEAN, TEXT_SINGLE_SELECT, or TEXT_MULTI_SELECT that controls whether this question is shown.

equals.description: For a BOOLEAN controlling question: show when the answer equals this value.

is_one_of.description: For a select controlling question: show when the answer is one of these choice labels.

section_id.description: Section to add to, from the target form (intake.sections or change_request_intake.sections) in get_spend_program_editor_state. Defaults to the first section.

position.description: Zero-based index within the section. Defaults to the end.

question_id.description: id from the target form (intake.sections or change_request_intake.sections) in get_spend_program_editor_state.

choices.description: Replacement choices, in order. Pass { id, label } with an id from the target form's sections to keep or rename an existing choice so visibility and required-when rules that depend on it keep working; pass a bare string to add a new choice. Existing choices left out are removed; removal is rejected when another question's or section's rule depends on the choice. The type cannot change.

id.description: Choice id from the target form (intake.sections or change_request_intake.sections) in get_spend_program_editor_state. Ids change when the user saves, so read them from the same editor_revision you write against.

visible_when.description: Replace the visibility rule; null always shows the question.

anyOf.description: Show this question only when an earlier answer matches.

equals.description: For a BOOLEAN controlling question: show when the answer equals this value.

automatic_issuance_rules.description: Who receives funds automatically when not everyone. Requires a FIXED funds amount. A non-empty list turns automatic issuance on; an empty list turns it off.

program_rules.description: Program-level rules that apply regardless of outcome.

allowed_overage_percent.description: Percent a requester may exceed the approved amount by; null disables overage.

spend_allocation_spend_intent_type.description: FIXED: admin sets amount and interval. CUSTOM_AMOUNT_FIXED_FREQUENCY: requester chooses the amount, admin fixes the interval. CUSTOM_AMOUNT_AND_FREQUENCY: requester chooses both.

amount.description: Fund limit in major currency units. Required when the type is FIXED.

interval.description: How often the limit resets. TOTAL is a one-time total; CUSTOM lets the requester choose. Required unless the type is CUSTOM_AMOUNT_AND_FREQUENCY.

requestable_frequency_once.description: Each employee may receive these funds only once.

transaction_amount_limit.description: Maximum single transaction amount; null means no per-transaction limit.

issue_physical_card_if_needed.description: Ship a physical card to employees who do not have one.

start_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Only allow spend on or after this date; must be before lock_date when one is set. null allows spend as soon as funds are issued.

lock_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Do not allow spend on or after this date; must be after start_date and after today. Changing it clears relative_lock_duration_count, so change only one of the two per call; null removes a fixed lock date.

auto_create_fund_if_payee_accepts_card.description: Issue funds automatically when the payee accepts card payments.

tools.description: Apply one filter to a visible, operable table. First call list_table_filters for this exact table_key and use its category_key and valueHint. For a listbox with searchable options, then call list_table_filter_options and pass returned labels in "values"; do not use value, filter_value, or option IDs. The parameters depend on the category's "kind": listbox → "values" (add "exclude" only where supported). date_range → "start_date"/"end_date" (YYYY-MM-DD, either alone for open-ended) or "last_period". amount_form (e.g. Amount) → "min" and/or "max" as plain numbers in major currency units: "over $3k" = min 3000, "under $500" = max 500. free_text → "text". currency → "text" with the currency code. If a call returns table_missing, table_hidden, or table_read_only, follow recovery_guidance and the live available_tables snapshot rather than repeating discovery or the failed call. Never substitute another dataset without user confirmation. Rebuild a call at most once after the target becomes available; if it fails again, explain the blocker.

table_key.description: The tableKey of a currently visible table. Available table keys are included in the message context and from list_page_tables.

text.description: Value for free_text or currency categories.

min.description: Minimum amount for amount_form categories, in major currency units (e.g. 3000 for $3,000). Omit for no minimum.

max.description: Maximum amount for amount_form categories, in major currency units. Omit for no maximum.

exclude.description: Invert the filter to exclude the given values (listbox categories that support it).
